By Mike Allen · Nov 23, 2026

☕️ Good Monday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 665 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Nvidia comeback shocker
 
Photo illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Photo: Tomohiro Ohsumi/Getty Images

Nvidia's stunning decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang sent the company's stock skyrocketing, yanked the broader market out of correction territory, and raised existential questions over the president's role in decision-making at the biggest company in the economy's most vital sector.

Nvidia's board said it was satisfied with Huang's "candor and ability to lead" after a series of meetings, Axios' Emily Peck and Madison Mills report.

  • Huang said in a statement: "I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution."
  • CFO Colette Kress, who had been serving as interim CEO, will return to her previous responsibilities.

🇨🇳 Huang's return comes 11 days after Nvidia announced his resignation, and 15 days after he admitted to an affair. U.S. national security agencies believe the affair was with a woman who is "believed to be a Chinese intelligence asset and who was also believed to be involved in possible illegal smuggling of Nvidia chips into China," the N.Y. Times reports.

  • Huang is set to testify publicly before Congress on Dec. 3 over his relationships and questions about Nvidia's business practices — including whether it did enough to stop its advanced AI chips from ending up in China.
Images: Donald J. Trump/Truth Social

📺 President Trump said he was directly involved in Huang's resurrection, telling CNBC this morning that "my intervention was very important." (Watch clip.)

  • Trump later posted a meme (above) imagining Huang surviving the 2024 assassination attempt against the president, with the CEO holding a red bra as an Nvidia flag waves in the background.

📈 Nvidia shares are up 30% as of midafternoon.

  • The tech-heavy Nasdaq is up 6.2%, while the S&P 500 is up 4.6%.

What's next: Huang may now be beyond reproach, Axios' Nathan Bomey writes.

  • Peter Jaworski, a business ethics professor at Georgetown University, tells Axios: "If he can get away with this, what constraints can the board put on his behavior?"

Go deeper.
 
 
2. 🎤 Gov. Moore rips Trump's Nvidia intervention
 
Mike Allen interviews Maryland Gov. Wes Moore today. Photo: JaMar Jones/Axios

Maryland Gov. Wes Moore (D) criticized President Trump's involvement in Nvidia's decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang, calling it "troubling and problematic" in an interview for "The Axios Show."

📺 Moore — chair of the National Governors Association and a potential 2028 presidential candidate — told Axios' Mike Allen in an interview at the Maryland State House in Annapolis today, just minutes after the news broke:

  • "The president is not a board member of Nvidia. So why he is involved in board dealings, I have no idea. ... It seems like it's rules for me, but not for thee."
  • "You have the wealthy and the powerful and the well-connected that are now making decisions to reinstate, where, frankly, if that was any of us, we would be held to a different type of standard."

4. 🦃 1 for the road: Don't forget to thaw
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

Thanksgiving is just a few days away — so don't forget to start thawing your turkey, if you bought a frozen bird.

  • The USDA recommends 24 hours of fridge thawing for every 4–5 pounds of turkey.

🍗 Another tip: "Keep the turkey in its original packaging and place it on a tray or in a container to catch any juices."

  • Cold-water thawing is a faster option — but you should cook your turkey right when it's ready to go.
